reviews.note: Two years after the first digital dollar statement, he attaches a pace ('freight train rate') and a vehicle: the budget bill.
Frames US debt near $40tn as past recovery, and widens the claim from America to the world.
Adds the global figure of $352tn and names what it is gearing toward.
The most decision-relevant economic claim in the corpus: a boom he expects to be real but terminal. Note it predicts good conditions first, which is unusual for him.
Anchors the window to legislation expiring in 2028, which is the only structural (rather than revelatory) date he gives for the good period.
Restates the 2023 fifty-cents-on-the-dollar figure unchanged, two years on. The number has never moved.
Quoting someone else on a CBDC being written into a deal. Kept as unsure because it is another person's assertion carried on his channel, not his vision.
Rare calibrated claim: he explicitly calls the wave shallow rather than catastrophic, which is falsifiable in both directions.
Carries a real window, May to the November 2026 midterms, so it becomes scoreable this year.

He claims the silver move he foresaw has arrived at an all-time high, referring back to the number he gave. This is a fulfilment assertion inside the thread, and is why the $75 target still needs scoring separately.
News commentary on Bitcoin's price rather than a claim of his own. Kept in the database, assigned to nothing.
October 2025 restatement of the shaking, widened from America to the earth, three weeks before the tariff-conditional version.
